artifacts.summary: 6-phase, 4-wave plan qualifying the verification-tier tie-break across four planning surfaces, introducing a required conditional **Tier Justification** field on non-final phases; the plan is its own acceptance demonstration.

memory_candidates.content: Two planning-layer traps when writing a phase-position-conditional verification rule in this agent system. (1) A rule conditioned on 'the final phase' is uncheckable until 'final phase' is defined: plan-format.md:273-277 and planner-agent.md:227 both use the term as if operational but nothing defines it. The workable definition is the plan's highest-numbered phase, required to be a terminal node of the dependency graph AND to depend transitively on every other phase -- the transitivity requirement is what makes the final full gate meaningful (it must observe all the task's work) and it removes the ambiguity of a last wave holding two mutually independent terminal phases. (2) scripts/lib/suite-selection-lib.sh's suite_selection_select returns the __FULL_SWEEP__ zero-hit sentinel for pure-documentation paths (verified: agents/planner-agent.md, context/workflows/task-breakdown.md, context/contracts/phase-closure.md all return it; only context/formats/plan-format.md maps to real suites). So a cheap verification tier on a markdown-guidance edit cannot honestly cite a covering shell suite at all -- the honest covering check is a gate subset (verify-deploy.sh --only-gate 3,4, doc-lint plus task-reference lint), not a suite subset. Guidance that offers only run-all.sh --only as the cheap-tier mechanism pushes every docs phase back to full.
